agitator.titleStart: Let's be honest: building a website shouldn't feel like a
agitator.lede: Most small business owners we talk to are dealing with one of these three headaches:

points.title: The DIY Disaster
points.body: You tried to build it yourself, but it just doesn't look quite right.

points.title: The Disappearing Act
points.body: You hired a cheap freelancer, but now they won't answer emails.

points.title: The Digital Ghost Town
points.body: You have a website, but it's not bringing in leads.

agitator.turnTitle: It doesn't have to be this way.
agitator.turnBody: We give you a done-for-you service with a long-term partner you can actually reach.

process.title: How It Works: Getting Online is Easy.
process.lede: Three steps, no jargon, and no homework for you beyond a logo and a few details.

steps.title: Choose Your Plan
steps.body: Pick one of our transparent, upfront website packages starting at just $499. No hidden fees, no surprises.

steps.title: We Build It
steps.body: Hand over your logo and a few details. We'll design a modern, mobile-friendly site tailored to your brand.

steps.title: We Maintain It
steps.body: Once we launch, you have total peace of mind. Choose the monthly Care Plan that fits your business, starting at $69/mo, and we will handle your premium hosting, security updates, and daily backups so you never have to worry.

process.imageAlt: Hands typing at a keyboard beside a navy notebook and an orange pen

caseStudy.title: See What A Great Website Can Do.
caseStudy.paragraph1: came to us with an awkward problem: two legally separate companies, one for insurance and one for tax and business services, that had to live under one roof without confusing customers or blurring the line between them.
caseStudy.paragraph2: We built a bilingual site that opens in English or Spanish, splits the two businesses into clear side-by-side paths, and carries the compliance wording each one needs. The phone number stays one tap away on every screen, because in their business the call is the conversion.

pricing.integrityNote: Ongoing care and maintenance plans are a separate, required service to keep your site secure and are not included in the one-time base website build price.

care.title: Ongoing Peace of Mind: Your Monthly Care Plan.
care.lede: A website is like a car: it needs regular maintenance to run smoothly. That is why every site we build requires a Care Plan, billed monthly from $69 on top of your build price. You choose the level that fits you.
care.note: Annual billing saves 15%. Care plans run for an initial 12 months from launch.

plans.name: Essential Care
plans.tagline: Everything your site needs to stay safe and online.
features: Up to 30 mins of text or photo changes

plans.name: Full Care
plans.tagline: Our most popular plan, more hands-on with faster answers.
features: Up to 1 hr of updates per month

plans.name: Premium Care
plans.tagline: For businesses that change their site often.
features: Up to 2 hrs of updates per month

care.imageAlt: A bright, calm studio office with a navy sofa and an orange book

items.q: Do I own my website and domain name?
items.a: 100%. You own your domain name and your website content. If you ever decide to move on after your initial 12-month care plan, you can take it all with you.

items.q: Are domain name and hosting included?
items.a: Premium hosting is fully included in all of our Care Plans. For your domain name, you will purchase and own this directly through a registrar like GoDaddy. We will handle all the technical work of connecting it to your new website for you.

items.q: Why do I need a monthly care plan?
items.a: Websites are not set it and forget it. Things break, software gets outdated, and hackers look for vulnerabilities. Our care plans ensure your site is hosted, protected, backed up, and updated every month.

mobile.title: Most of your customers will find you on a phone.
mobile.lede: Every site we build is designed for the small screen first, then scaled up. Not the other way round, which is how sites end up unreadable in the place they get used most.
